title: Low Power Protection Act
official_summary:
Low Power Protection Act

This bill provides for a one-year period during which eligible low-power television stations may apply to the Federal Communications Commission (FCC) for Class A licenses. To be eligible, a station must serve a media market with a limited number of television households, broadcast a minimum number of hours, and meet other requirements.

A low-power station with a Class A license obtains certain broadcast rights, including primary status with respect to its allocation of the electromagnetic spectrum. (Typically, low-power stations have secondary status and may be displaced from their spectrum in the event the FCC reallocates it to a primary user.)

summary.headline: A 2023 law opens a one-year window for eligible low-power TV stations to apply to the FCC for Class A licenses, which give stronger spectrum protection.
summary.what_it_does: The law sets up a one-year period in which eligible low-power television stations can apply to the Federal Communications Commission for Class A licenses. To qualify, a station must serve a media market with a limited number of TV households, broadcast a minimum number of hours, and meet other requirements. A station with a Class A license gets primary status over its spectrum, while low-power stations usually have secondary status and can be moved if the FCC reassigns that spectrum to a primary user.

who_it_affects.how: Stations that meet the market and broadcast requirements can apply during the one-year window to receive Class A status and its primary spectrum rights.

who_it_affects.group: Low-power stations that do not qualify or do not apply
who_it_affects.how: They keep their existing secondary status and can still be displaced if the FCC reallocates their spectrum to a primary user.
The agency must process applications from stations seeking Class A licenses during the window.

summary.when_it_takes_effect: The law was enacted on January 5, 2023. The official summary does not list the exact start and end dates of the one-year application window.
